newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea arrests "National Liberation Army" students.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea arrests "National Liberation Army" students.

text.p: Twenty-four South Korean students accused of being members of a pro-North Korean "National Liberation Army" were arrested on Wednesday, prosecution officials said.
The students have been charged under the National Security law that guards against subversion from rival North Korea.
Prosecutors allege the "army" is a branch of a radical student council, the Hanchongryon, that led violent protests in support of Korean unification at Seoul's Yonsei University in August.
The students were rounded up on five college campuses in South Cholla province, a traditional hotbed of political dissent and home of South Korea's most famous opposition politician, Kim Dae-jung.

"The 24 students had been under investigation and were detained early today after arrest warrants were issued by the district court," said a prosecution official, speaking by telephone from Kwangju in Cholla province.
Lee Moo-young, Cholla's top police officer, was quoted by the state-run Korea Broadcasting System as saying 95 of an estimated 800 members of the group had been arrested since January.
About 130 members attended a hidden training camp in July to practice with molotov cocktails for attacks on policemen and police facilities, Lee said.

In August riot police stormed Yonsei University to end a seven-day student occupation of two teaching blocks following an annual rally demanding Korean unification and the withdrawal of 37,000 U.S. troops stationed in South Korea.

A total of 444 students have gone on trial for their roles in the demonstrations in which one policeman died and hundreds of officers and students were injured. So far, 220 have been sentenced to jail or given suspended sentences.
The maximum punishment under the National Security law is death.
